target_customer: Landlords and property managers screening tenants, plus renters building credit through rent payments, in Canada and the US
problem: Landlords lacked reliable tenant screening and renters got no credit for paying rent on time. Naborly built rental credit reports and scores and later a lease guarantee product.
business_model: Per-report screening fees (14.99 to 24.99 dollars per report per a review site), later free US screening plus a premium Canadian tier and a lease guarantee product
product_category: Tenant screening and rental credit bureau

founders.name: Dylan Lenz
education: BASc Computer Engineering, UBC (per YC page)
PhD, University of Toronto, as the YC page states it
founders.background_notes: YC page describes background in product design, business development and growth. The PhD line on the YC page reads oddly and was recorded as written.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed credit bureau data integrations (it later partnered with Equifax Canada) and a scoring model, which is standard engineering with some data access hurdles.

defensibility.rationale: Screening reports were reproducible from bureau partners and many rivals existed. Rental payment data could have built a data asset but no source shows it did.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Bureaus ran their own tenant screening products. Naborly was ultimately bought by a smaller direct competitor, SingleKey, in 2022, which shut down the Naborly technology.

market_need_then: Landlords already paid for screening and renters often could not build credit from rent. Naborly reported serving over 850,000 rental units by late 2019 per BetaKit. No 2018 spend figure was found.

branding.domain_note: naborly.com, an exact .com, which now redirects to singlekey.com after the 2022 acquisition.

identity.mascot_or_character: Its AI system was named SHERLY per a BetaKit report on the LRANK deal

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name was shut down on acquisition and users moved to SingleKey.

pivots.from: Rental credit bureau and screening reports
pivots.to: Free screening plus NaborlyShield lease and rent guarantee product
pivots.why: BetaKit says per-report pricing was dropped and the seed round funded NaborlyShield to replace deposits and co-signers

outcome_analysis: Naborly raised a small first seed and then a 7.5 million dollar seed in 2019 and expanded from screening into a guarantee product. By 2022 it had raised 13.5 million dollars in total per BetaKit and was sold to its competitor SingleKey, which kept few employees, shut the Naborly technology and tried to make investors and lenders whole. That reads as a soft landing after a failure to reach a larger round, though no source states the cause directly, so the factor is recorded as other.
notes: BetaKit says 13.5 million dollars was raised in total but only about 8.75 million is itemized, so other rounds or debt are missing. The 1.25 million seed date is not stated in the source. The 7.5 million USD equals 9.9 million CAD. Aggregators list a 2016 angel round of about 1 million; unverified and not recorded. The company site now redirects to SingleKey. A dated 2018 competitor search returned only current aggregator lists, so the list is empty. Sources conflict on headquarters (Toronto vs San Francisco).
